metadata.description: Likely represents the domain for cookies used by the UI.
metadata.usage: Should be set to the domain where cookies are valid, e.g., 'example.com'.

suggestions: Ensure this is set to a valid domain if cookies are used in the application.
If not required, clarify its purpose and remove unused variables.

metadata.description: Represents the name of the cookie used by the UI.
metadata.usage: Typically used to identify a specific session or tracking cookie.

suggestions: Assign a meaningful cookie name to avoid conflicts and ensure proper functionality.
If unused, consider removing this variable.

metadata.description: Indicates the type of login/authentication mechanism used by the UI.

suggestions: Ensure that the login type matches the authentication provider configured for the system.
Document valid options for this variable to avoid misconfiguration.

metadata.description: Represents a password used for site access. This is sensitive information.
metadata.security: Should be stored securely using encryption or secret management systems.

suggestions: Move this value to a secure secrets manager (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault).
Avoid hardcoding sensitive credentials in environment variables.
Rotate this password regularly to enhance security.

metadata.description: Represents the username or email used for site access. This is sensitive information.

suggestions: Store this value securely using secret management systems.
Avoid exposing email addresses in environment variables to minimize risk of leakage.
Consider using role-based accounts instead of individual email addresses for automation tools.
